stories.headline: Man City chairman on club's Premier League charges case: 'Nothing has changed'
stories.summary: Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has said "nothing has changed" regarding the club's ongoing legal battle with the Premier League.
stories.body:
Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has said "nothing has changed" regarding the club's ongoing legal battle with the Premier League, adding "our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began."

City are expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League, a source confirmed to ESPN.

In a statement on Friday, City didn't deny the guilty verdicts and said that the process "remains ongoing."

When contacted by ESPN on Friday, the Premier League said it wouldn't comment on a "private and confidential process."

It is expected that City -- who could face anything from a fine to a points deduction or even expulsion from the Premier League by way of punishment -- will appeal any guilty verdict.

Sources: Premier League clubs seeking legal advice over Man City charges

Al Mubarak's statement read: "I have been part of this Club for 18 years. I have had the privilege to stand with you in the Etihad, at Wembley, and in Istanbul. This Club matters to me, and you have shown and told me -- time and time again -- how much Manchester City matters to you," he said in a statement published on City's website.

"This is why I am writing to you today. Following Friday's media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues. So have I. Here's what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the Club's innocence is just as strong as when this began.

"There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies.

"I ask you to please carefully read the statement below, which we gave on Friday, and the statement we issued in February 2023. Every word matters and holds true.

"While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our Club. We will not give them that opportunity.

"We have some exciting moments to look forward to after this international break. We travel to Anfield in a fortnight, and then host Paris St Germain in the Champions League back at Etihad Stadium -- moments that give us an opportunity to celebrate the strength of the Manchester City family.

"Thank you, as always, for your constant support."

Ogden: Man City verdict will leave a stain and stench on a Premier League era

The Premier League announced the charges against City in February 2023 following a four-year investigation.

The case was heard at an independent hearing at the International Dispute Resolution Centre in London, beginning in September 2024. It came to an end in December 2024 after 12 weeks of deliberations.

The alleged breaches of financial rules were said to have occurred over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.

The Premier League's claim was centered around its belief that City did not provide "accurate financial information that gives a true and fair view of the club's financial position."

City have maintained their innocence throughout the process.

stories.headline: Mauricio Pochettino: Cavan Sullivan ready for USMNT debut
stories.summary: USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino said 16-year-old phenom Cavan Sullivan is ready to play for the USMNT during the current international window, but was non-committal as to what role he would play in Saturday's friendly against Peru.
stories.body:
ORLANDO -- United States men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino said 16-year-old phenom Cavan Sullivan is ready to play for the USMNT during the current international window, but was noncommittal as to what role he would play in Saturday's friendly against Peru.

Sullivan has garnered the most attention on the current squad, even as 13 players that were part of the World Cup are also on the current roster.

This is due not only to his age, but also his recent performances for the Philadelphia Union, which have seen him score six goals and add eight assists in his last eight league games.

That has led to a tidal wave of anticipation to see what Sullivan can do at international level.

Pochettino said earlier this month that he and the staff needed to be "careful" in how they manager the young attacker. He was circumspect in his assessment of Sullivan at Friday's pre-match news conference.

"If we only talk about his performance, he's doing really well in his club in Philadelphia. Talking only about that, I think he's ready, but the rest of the players too," Pochettino said about Sullivan. "He's mature enough on the field."

Pochettino also praised the entire group for how they performed in training this week, and lauded the vitality that the youngsters have brought to the group.

"They have talent, and they are showing the real talent," Pochettino said of the young players. "They have an amazing capacity and quality. And then the energy was amazing. It's very contagious, that energy."

Pochettino added that he will use a mix of youth and experience against Peru, and he'll take the data from training to determine who is ready to play and who isn't.

"When we observe the player, maybe some players need more time, maybe not to play the first game or the second, maybe the third or maybe some player training with us is enough and maybe they don't need to go to play," Pochettino said. "I think it's so important to provide the chance if they are ready."

The USMNT manager said he'll be looking at a variety of other factors as well in terms of deciding what constitutes "ready."

He indicated he's been spending much of the week getting to know the players off the field as well as on. He's observed how the new players adapt to the environment, especially when the staff sets the tone early.

"I think if the young kids arrive in an environment that they smell respect, they smell the discipline, the normal discipline in a team that plays soccer, I think they are very natural," he said.

"I think what we need to, that was our plan is to create an environment that they can feel natural. We want them to behave in a natural way because they are intelligent, they're smart and they perceive and feel in the way that they need to act when they arrive."

Pochettino's assessment included getting the young players to get up on stage at a team dinner, one at a time, and sing a song in front of the team and staff.

"In all these types of things, you start to see their personality, their character, capacity to move," Pochettino said. "And then when they start to train, how the senior players respect them and start to play together and see how they move, how they talk, how they communicate, that's key. Then of course you need to talk with them and say, you feel that you are ready or not? But I think it's good to ask them, but at the same time it's to perceive and to read all this type of situation to be sure that they can go."

stories.headline: Lando Norris: Drivers should have 'one-race ban' after collision with Franco Colapinto at Azerbaijan GP
stories.summary: Lando Norris has said there are "drivers that shouldn't be in Formula 1" and that Franco Colapinto should be banned for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix pile-up which ended his race.
stories.body:
Lando Norris has said there are "drivers that shouldn't be in Formula 1" and that Franco Colapinto should be banned for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix pile-up which ended his race.

Colapinto wiped out Norris and his own Alpine teammate Pierre Gasly from the race at a Safety Car restart on lap 36, locking up and going down the inside of Turn 1.

Norris had dropped down the order with a lock-up of his own earlier in the race, leaving him battling in the midfield at the restart.

The reigning world champion pointed the finger of blame at Colapinto, hinting that the Argentine driver does not deserve his spot on the grid.

"I was just slow," Norris told Sky Sports after the Baku race. "Struggled a lot in this race. You saw how quickly everyone came past me.

"Otherwise, I still made the mistake. But at the end of the day, I just got taken out. Just some drivers that shouldn't be in Formula 1 to, be honest."

Colaptino was handed a 10-second time penalty for the incident, and was later given a five-place grid penalty for the next race in Malaysia, as he did not make it to the end of the race.

He and teammate Gasly had been running strongly -- after the incident, Gasly was broadcast saying: "Oh my god. Oh my god. I cannot believe it. So many [censored] points gone!"

Speaking to the written press, Norris doubled down, suggesting Colapinto should be banned for the next race.

As quoted by PA, Norris said: "If you cause a crash on a restart like this, you should have at least a one-race ban.

"I just got taken out. And the FIA should be stricter by starting to hand out bans for this kind of stuff.

- Azerbaijan Grand Prix: George Russell fights off Max Verstappen to take dominant win

- Max Verstappen says he prefers F1 not to race in Middle East due to ongoing conflict

- Azerbaijan Grand Prix results: George Russell takes commanding victory in Baku - as it happened

"It is just careless. It costs a lot of money, all my parts are in the bin now. It is not driving that deserves to be in Formula 1.

"In Formula 1 you would expect that drivers can anticipate that the grip will be low and tyre temperatures are low.

"You want to be against the best drivers and when stuff like this happens it is because, yeah, they shouldn't be there."

Colapinto, who was recently given an Alpine contract extension for 2027, accepted responsibility, apologising to his team and teammate, as well as Norris.

"Just sorry to all the team, not only to Pierre, it was a big mistake," Colapinto said. "Big sorry to Pierre, he has been working really hard in the factory. We lost a lot of positions and we were with both cars in the points.

"Very sad and disappointed. Big, big sorry, it's a big mistake. Cold brakes, cold tyres, I was completely out of control. Unfortunately, I also took Pierre out. And Lando of course. Big sorry to both of them."

The incident might raise fears of what the social media backlash will be.

Ahead of the weekend, Gasly revealed the threats he, his girlfriend and family members had received after he held up Colapinto in the closing stages of the Madrid Grand Prix.

Colapinto has built a big fanbase back home in Argentina since his debut in 2024.

Asked about the partnership with Gasly, Colapinto said: "We are good. We've always been quite good together. Since we worked together for the first time, we got on very well. So we need to move on."

Gasly appeared unmoved when told about Colapinto's apology, reflecting on the big points loss in the championship.

"I can't find my words," Gasly said. "It's not easy. We did a very good weekend and the car was one of the best race cars we've had this season. And the pace was great. Keeping up with Lewis [Hamilton] and Lando for most of the race. And we had a 14 or 15 second gap to the midfield."

When asked if the partnership was still in a good place, Gasly said: "Respect. It's all about respect. As long as there is respect, everything is possible."

Speaking in the top-three news conference about Norris' comments, race winner George Russell disagreed with the fellow Brit.

Russell said: "Yeah, I think that's too harsh, personally. I think Safety Car restarts, cold tyres, a very small mistake can have big consequences. And from what I saw today, that's what it looked like. It was a small error that had a big consequence. I think, personally, race bans should come from drivers intentionally doing something very dangerous and very reckless. So I think it was unfortunate."

Four-time world champion Max Verstappen agreed with Russell and added: "Yeah, I think as long [as], of course, the driver that caused it is aware of what he did, right, and apologised. And, I mean, yeah, that happens.

"I mean, like, a small mistake or misjudgement, you lock up, it's on the inside, low grip, and, of course, then I guess a bit unfortunate that it involves so many cars. But, yeah, unfortunate, happens, and it's not nice, I think. Not nice for anyone involved, right? But like George said, I think, yeah, a race ban probably is a bit much."

stories.headline: What to watch during MLB's final weekend of the 2026 season
stories.summary: There's still much to play for entering the final days of the regular season. We have your guide to the last few games of baseball before October.
stories.body:
We have two days left in the 2026 MLB regular season -- and still have several playoff races and seeds to decide, including two division races. The Chicago White Sox clinched a playoff spot on Thursday, making them perhaps the most shocking playoff team since the 2008 Tampa Bay Rays. But they still have their sights on a division title.

Across town, the Chicago Cubs also punched their ticket -- the first time the two clubs have ever clinched playoff berths on the same day, according to ESPN Research -- as Pete Crow-Armstrong became the seventh member of the 40/40 club. PCA has the NL MVP Award locked up, but he can still add the NL home run title to his ledger of awesomeness. Chicago baseball fans can now officially dream of the first White Sox-Cubs World Series since 1906.

Let's run down what's at stake this weekend, in the playoff races and on the individual side.

Playoff races

AL Central

Cleveland Guardians: 84-76 (at Kansas City Royals)

Chicago White Sox: 83-77 (vs. Colorado Rockies)

Tiebreaker: White Sox over Guardians

This has been a fun race over the past 10 days or so, since the pair played an exciting series last week. Both teams have continued to play well. The Guardians won six in a row before a 1-0 loss Wednesday, and a tired White Sox pitching staff delivered three one-run games last weekend against the Tigers.

Winning the division is important here: The winner will get the No. 2 seed and a bye into the division series and be able to rest its pitchers for a few days, which is especially important for a White Sox bullpen that has been pitching a ton of innings. Closer Grant Taylor, for example, has pitched more than one inning in his past five appearances, including one outing of seven outs. At least he has had five days off since last pitching Saturday, so he's ready to go for Chicago this weekend.

The Guardians have Tanner Bibee starting on Saturday and then Parker Messick if needed on Sunday. If the Guardians don't win the division, that would leave Foster Griffin as the likely Game 1 starter in the wild-card series, with Williams ready to go in Game 2. That's not an ideal scenario given Griffin has a 5.19 ERA since coming to Cleveland at the trade deadline.

The White Sox line up Davis Martin and Anthony Kay in the final two games against the Rockies.

NL wild card
San Diego Padres: 89-71 (vs. Arizona Diamondbacks)

Chicago Cubs: 88-72 (at Boston Red Sox)

Philadelphia Phillies: 87-73 (vs. Tampa Bay Rays)

Arizona Diamondbacks: 86-74 (at Padres)

Tiebreakers:

• Cubs over Padres, Phillies and Diamondbacks

• Phillies over Padres

• Diamondbacks over Phillies

OK, this got a little less complicated with the Padres' win over the Dodgers on Thursday as they joined the Cubs in clinching a playoff spot. Arizona, with six wins in a row, remains alive. The Diamondbacks will need more help from the Rays, but if they finish tied with the Phillies, they're in and the Phillies out.

The above tiebreakers are just the head-to-head tiebreakers for a two-way tie. If three or more clubs are tied, it goes to winning percentage in games against one another. The Cubs won the season series against all three opponents, which is why they've clinched. If the Cubs, Phillies and Diamondbacks finish 88-74, the Cubs are the fifth seed while the Diamondbacks are the sixth seed. If the Cubs, Phillies and Padres finish tied, the Cubs are the fourth seed, the Phillies fifth and the Padres sixth.

AL West
Texas Rangers: 79-81 (at Minnesota Twins)

Houston Astros: 79-81 (at Athletics)

Tiebreaker: Astros over Rangers

Yes, dear readers, we might get our first sub-.500 division champion. It probably would have happened in the AL West in 1994, when the Rangers were 52-62, but the strike hit. For now, the worst record for a division winner belongs to the 2005 Padres, who won the NL West with an 82-80 record. This has been the division nobody wants to win: The Rangers are 11-10 in September after their win Thursday, and the Astros are 8-12.

The weekend's starting pitchers:

Rangers: Nathan Eovaldi, undecided

Astros: Hayden Wesneski, undecided

Neither team will be in great shape with its starting pitchers entering the wild-card series after Hunter Brown and Jacob deGrom both lost Friday's series openers. Cal Quantrill had been pitching great for the Rangers but injured his lat in his last start and landed on the 60-day IL. Cristian Javier would be slated to start Sunday for the Astros, but he left his start Tuesday after two innings. Kumar Rocker for the Rangers and Peter Lambert for the Astros would be the guys to start Game 1 since they pitched Thursday.

NL's top teams
Milwaukee Brewers: 101-59 (vs. St. Louis Cardinals)

Los Angeles Dodgers: 98-62 (at San Francisco Giants)

Tiebreakers: Brewers over Dodgers

The Brewers clinched the No. 1 seed Thursday with a win and a loss by the Dodgers; the Braves' loss to the Reds on Thursday locked them into the No. 3 seed and clinched a bye for the Dodgers.

How has the top overall seed done in the postseason? Though baseball's playoffs are widely regarded as having a more random nature than other sports', over the past 10 seasons, four of the top teams did win the World Series and two others reached it. Of course, there have always been the anomalies -- like in 2021, when the Braves won it all after finishing the regular season with the 12th-best record in the majors, or 2023, when we had a World Series matchup between the Rangers (tied for sixth-best record) and Diamondbacks (tied for 12th).

Here's what this weekend's starters look like for each team:

Brewers: Dustin May, Jacob Misiorowski

Dodgers: Blake Snell, undecided

Braves: Martin Perez, JR Ritchie

Misiorowski last pitched Sunday, when he threw 44 pitches in three innings while pitching on four days' rest for the first time since July 7. The first game of the NLDS won't be until Oct. 3, so that would give him five days of rest before his Game 1 start. Like his last outing, this might be an abbreviated one to keep him as fresh as possible for that first October game.

Of note: The NL division series schedules have one less off day than the AL series, with off days after Games 2 and 4, so Misiorowski probably would return in a potential Game 5, pitching on five days' rest. In the AL, the Game 1 starter could return for Game 4 on four days' rest. For the Brewers, that also means they will need four starters in the NLDS, when only Misiorowski and Logan Henderson look dependable right now. May has been pulled in the third inning of his past two starts, which could push Gasser into the No. 3 role (Kyle Harrison looks like a complete nonfactor right now).

Keep in mind that the Brewers used an opener in four of their nine playoff games last year, so that's a possibility -- although the more likely scenario is that manager Pat Murphy has quick hooks with Gasser and May and relies on his bullpen.

Statistical races

Yordan Alvarez tries to lock up MVP

This was a Triple Crown chase a few weeks ago, but Pete Alonso pretty much clinched the RBI title and now leads in home runs as well, so the Astros slugger probably will have to settle for the MVP Award instead. The question: Do the Astros need to win the division for Alvarez to win? I don't think so. Though we're likely to see a scattered vote, with Alvarez, Junior Caminero, Bobby Witt Jr. and maybe Cam Schlittler all receiving first-place votes, Alvarez is probably the only player who is going to land first or second on just about every ballot.

Caminero has the advantage of having Drew Rasmussen and Nick Martinez as teammates on the mound, while Alvarez had Mike Burrows and Tatsuya Imai. But as hitters, Alvarez has been much better: He has created an estimated 151 runs heading into Thursday's games compared with 107 for Caminero (who also ranks behind Ben Rice, Alonso and Miguel Vargas). And since Alvarez has the much higher on-base percentage -- .432 to .360 -- and Caminero has also grounded into 26 double plays, Alvarez has created more runs while using far fewer outs. He's the best hitter in baseball this year, and it's not close. That should get him MVP honors.

Who will finish with the most home runs?

AL: Alonso hit two home runs and Friday to take a two-homer leader over Alvarez, Caminero and Rice. The last home run tie came in 2021, when Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and Salvador Perez led the AL with 48. There has never been a three-way tie ... but there was a four-way tie in the AL in the strike-shortened season of 1981, when Eddie Murray, Dwight Evans, Bobby Grich and Tony Armas all hit 22.

NL: Crow-Armstrong and Kyle Schwarber are tied with 45. Schwarber is looking to lead the league for the second straight season and the third time since he joined the Phillies in 2022.

Who wins the batting title?

AL: Alvarez (.315) and Chandler Simpson (.306) are the only AL batters hitting .300.

NL: Gabriel Moreno (.311) passed Luis Arraez (.310), with Otto Lopez (.304) needing a super finish. Arraez, who left Thursday's game with a sprained ankle and will likely miss at least the weekend, is going for his fourth batting crown, and Moreno would be the first catcher to lead since Buster Posey in 2012.

Will Alonso make history?

If Alonso does hold on to his RBI lead, he'll become the first player to lead both leagues in RBIs after leading the NL with 131 in 2022 while with the Mets.

A few other races:

• NL RBIs: Alec Burleson (115) leads Sal Stewart (111) with Crow-Armstrong at 107. Not exactly the top contenders in March. Stewart would become the first rookie to lead his league since Walt Dropo of the 1950 Red Sox (some guy named Ted Williams is the only other rookie to do it).

• MLB strikeout leader: Cleveland's Williams passed Misiorowski and now leads, 248 to 247. Misiorowski leads Schlittler for the overall major league lead in ERA, 1.86 to 1.95.

• A swing and a miss: Colston Montgomery broke Mark Reynolds' single-season record of 223 strikeouts with his 224th on Friday. But Schwarber is close behind with 218 strikeouts.

Saying goodbye

This is the final weekend for Justin Verlander ... and maybe Max Scherzer?

Verlander has announced his retirement, so we know his start Saturday at Comerica Park will be the final one of his illustrious first-ballot Hall of Fame career. Verlander has made only one start for the Detroit Tigers this season after returning to the team that drafted him No. 2 in 2004 (the Padres selected Matt Bush in front of him, one of the biggest draft mistakes of all time).

The three-time Cy Young winner looked like a potential 300-game winner in 2019, when he had 225 wins through his age-36 season and was coming off a 21-win and Cy Young season for the Astros. But Verlander pitched only once in 2020 before his elbow surrendered to time and then he sat out all of 2021. Remarkably, he came back in 2022 and won another Cy Young Award with an 18-win season and career-low 1.75 ERA. At the time, 300 wins remained a possibility -- and a goal.

But he would go just 22-26 over the next four seasons, leaving him at 266 wins entering his final career start. After Scherzer and his 224 wins, next on the active wins list are Gerrit Cole at 163 and Chris Sale at 159. We're not only not going to see a 300-game winner for ... well, who knows ... but we might not even see a 200-game winner for a long time. Indeed, Verlander and Scherzer will go down as perhaps the last of the true old-school guys who pitched 200-plus innings -- and more at their peak -- year after year.

Scherzer, who has a 6.14 ERA in 17 starts this season, hasn't officially announced his retirement, recently saying he'll have an announcement on his future in the coming days. He just pitched Wednesday but might come back on short rest to make one final start at home for his Toronto Blue Jays on Sunday. Maybe he wants to try to pass his former teammate on the career strikeout list: Verlander is eighth with 3,554 strikeouts, while Scherzer is four behind at 3,550.

The two were teammates for five seasons in Detroit, where they had, let us say, a bit of a rivalry. Here's hoping Scherzer gets one last opportunity, if this is indeed the end, and finishes in a dead heat with Verlander. Then they can enter Cooperstown together.

stories.headline: Rio field gets final touches, 'no need to worry' NFL says
stories.summary: NFL field director Nick Pappas said Saturday that the league has made additional improvements to the Rio field and that "things check out" ahead of Sunday's game between the Ravens and Cowboys.
stories.body:
RIO DE JANEIRO -- Workers were still trimming the turf at Maracana Stadium on Saturday, less than 30 hours before the NFL's first game in Rio de Janeiro, which is between the Dallas Cowboys and the Baltimore Ravens.

Some were using scissors to level the high grass, an effort that should end hours before the game.

The Maracana's turf has been a concern for almost two weeks due to its poor shape amid a long season in Brazilian soccer. Local clubs, Flamengo and Fluminense, play there at least once a week.

Maracana workers were using mows and scissors, big and small, to perfect the turf for the game.

On Friday, the executive director of the NFL Players Association said both the NFL and the players' union have had experts monitoring the field conditions for Sunday's game. The union's experts are worried about loose turf leading to too much slipping.

Concerns are about the turf's traction and stability, which made the NFL reinforce its stitching. Earlier this week, field director Nick Pappas said he was confident players will have no trouble.

On Saturday, Pappas told journalists that the NFL made additional improvements since the union's concerns were raised.

"Things check out," Pappas said. "No need to worry."

The NFL has been playing in Brazil since 2024, but the two previous games were at the 48,000-seat NeoQuimica Arena in Sao Paulo. In the first year of the Brazil game, its turf was also criticized and forced players of the Philadelphia Eagles and the Green Bay Packers to change their cleats to stop slipping.

The Maracana field is 100% natural grass, while the NeoQuimica Arena has a mixture between natural and synthetic that footballers in Brazil deem to be the country's best pitch.

The Cowboys and Ravens began their preparations in Rio on Friday following roughly 10-hour flights and are expected to have their first visit to the stadium later on Saturday.

Their game Sunday will be one of a record nine international contests on the NFL schedule this season.

Outside the Maracana, locals and tourists seem to be keener to go to the beach at 80 degrees on Saturday than preparing for Sunday's game. Unlike Sao Paulo, Rio has a more touristic atmosphere that has drawn a new batch of football followers from South America.

"I came because of the NFL game, but I also came because of Rio," said Chilean tourist Juan Olmedo, 61, a fan of the Denver Broncos. "This game being here has that extra element it didn't have in Sao Paulo. Those who went to Sao Paulo were there for the game and not much else."

Tourist spots such as Sugar Loaf Mountain and the statue of Christ the Redeemer also welcomed American and local fans who are attending the game Sunday.

stories.headline: Man City verdict will leave a stain and stench on a Premier League era
stories.summary: Manchester City are expected to be found guilty of almost all 115 financial charges against them. It means an era of English soccer is now tarnished with multiple asterisks.
stories.body:
It was one of the Premier League's most iconic moments: May 2014 and Steven Gerrard, Liverpool's heroic captain, finally lifts the Premier League trophy alongside manager Brendan Rodgers, who ended the club's quarter-century wait to become champions of England once again. What a story.

England's fallen giants were back on their perch, and Gerrard, the greatest player never to win a title medal, was able to put the seal on a glorious career with the one major honor missing from his collection. Except it didn't happen. Just like Jose Mourinho winning his fourth Premier League title with Manchester United didn't happen four years later.

Perhaps in a parallel universe Liverpool are listed as 2013-14 Premier League champions and United in 2017-18, but in the real world, Manchester City came out on top on both occasions and on many more. But did they really?

The news that City are expected to be found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges related to breaching Premier League financial regulations between 2009 and 2018 -- neither City nor the Premier League deny the verdict of the independent panel -- means that everything they achieved during that period is now in question. City have consistently denied all the charges and are expected to appeal the verdict.

Forget the asterisks next to those title wins and cup triumphs -- those moments that have been imprinted forever on the fabric of English football. The imprints are still there -- they will never go away -- but neither will the stain and the stench of being found guilty of breaking the rules -- cheating -- to claim their own glorious moments and, just as importantly, deny others from experiencing them.

So next time you see a replay of Sergio Aguero's famous title-winning goal in the final seconds of the 3-2 win against Queen's Park Rangers on the final day of the 2011-12 season, ask yourself whether it is valid. Or more likely, the footage becomes nothing more than the Premier League's version of Ben Johnson sprinting to gold in the 1988 Olympics 100-meter final or any of the seven consecutive Tour de France wins by Lance Armstrong between 1999 and 2005.

Johnson and Armstrong were both unmasked as drug cheats and stripped of their titles. That may yet happen to City when the Premier League rolls out its sanctions for the industrial scale breaches that the club has been found guilty of -- massive fines and points deductions which could lead to relegation are likely -- but the problem is that nobody really remembers who came second in an unfair race.

Who did Armstrong beat into second place in those seven successive wins? Good luck answering that without using Wikipedia. But for those like Gerrard, Rodgers and Mourinho, finishing second to City had its costs and real-life consequences.

Gerrard would retire without ever having won the Premier League, and he has since admitted that his slip in a 2-0 home defeat against Chelsea, which tilted the title race in City's favour, still haunts him every day. Mourinho was fired by United months after finishing second to City in 2018 -- a feat he described at the time as his "greatest achievement" due to the power of his opponent -- while Rodgers never recovered from Liverpool's failure to win the title and was gone from Anfield just over a year later.

Former United defender Rio Ferdinand, part of the team that missed out on the title by goal difference to City in 2012, reacted to news of the 114 charges by saying, "Another Premier League medal to be added to the cabinet," while former teammate David de Gea, who finished second in 2012 and 2018, posted on X, "So...Let's talk. How many Premier League titles have I won then?"

But it goes deeper than clubs, players and managers who narrowly missed out in second place because City spent beyond their means, paying higher wages and transfer fees because of inflated sponsorship deals and off-the-books payments.

Arsenal arguably took a decade to recover from having their squad repeatedly raided by City in the early years of Abu Dhabi ownership, while United have never been the same powerhouse since Carlos Tevez left Old Trafford for City in the summer of 2009, sparking the club's rise to dominance.

Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger once used the phrase "financial doping" to describe Chelsea's lavish spending under Russian owner Roman Abramovich -- Mourinho benefited more than most with those millions building his back-to-back title-winning team at Stamford Bridge -- but City took it to a different level.

Arsenal were victims of the early spending spree at City, described at the time by then-CEO Garry Cook as the club's "accelerated acquisition strategy," with a succession of players being lured away from the Emirates for huge fees and salaries.

Kolo Toure, Emmanuel Adebayor, Bacary Sagna, Gael Clichy and Samir Nasri all made the move from Arsenal to City during the 2009-2018 period investigated by the Premier League.

Arsenal needed the money after borrowing funds to build the Emirates, but City -- a team that had not won a trophy since 1976 and had been in the third tier as recently as 1999 -- suddenly became a dream destination for players and, bankrolled by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al Nahyan, they ruthlessly raided Wenger's team time and again to build their own empire and diminish Arsenal's.

Arsenal have since recovered, becoming champions again last season under manager Mikel Arteta, who once worked as an assistant coach to Guardiola at City. However, even though the period between 2018 and the present day is not covered by the Premier League investigation, the power and prestige gained by City during that period -- they are the only English club with an unbroken Champions League qualification record since first playing in the competition in 2011 -- made them such a formidable rival for Arteta's team to overcome.

Would Guardiola, Erling Haaland, Rodri, Kevin De Bruyne, Aguero and so many more star names have chosen City over other clubs without the rule-breaking that allowed them to become the most successful team in the country? In a sport where money rules, the answer is an easy one to find.

Money has ruled, and City have prospered, but when the expected guilty verdict is made, their achievements will officially have been made by breaking the rules. The price on their ticket will now be a very heavy one.

It could mean a massive points deduction that could lead to relegation, huge fines that could financially ruin the club, sponsors deserting due to reputational damage, players wanting to leave, and those who don't might have to go anyway, their salaries no longer affordable.

City are likely to face legal action from rival clubs for loss of earnings, titles, European qualification and commercial revenue; the ramifications are endless. In 2024, Arsenal, Liverpool, United and Tottenham served legal notices on City, reserving the right to seek compensation if the club were found guilty of serious charges.

City's Abu Dhabi hierarchy may also be driven out of the game for overseeing the prolonged rule-breaking, which makes them unfit for office. If buying City in 2008 really was an Abu Dhabi sportswashing project, designed to polish the Gulf state's global brand, the end result was incalculable damage.

Yet even if Gerrard, Rodgers, Mourinho, Ferdinand, De Gea and the rest suddenly wake up one morning to the delivery of an overdue winners' medal, it won't make up for what happened at the time.

But if you never see Aguero's title-winning goal replayed on TV again, you now know why.

stories.headline: AFL Grand Final player ratings: Every Fremantle and Brisbane player graded
stories.summary: Who stepped up? Who went missing? We graded every player from Grand Final day.
stories.body:
How did every Brisbane and Fremantle player fare on AFL Grand Final day? We rate all 46 out of 10, with players listed in jumper number order.

Brisbane
1. Kai Lohmann, 8/10 -- A proven finals performer delivered again. Kicked two goals, while his clean hands led to majors for Oscar Allen and Levi Ashcroft. Also laid a career-high 10 tackles.

2. Sam Draper, 5/10 -- Didn't allow Dockers star Luke Jackson to dominate in the way we all know he can. Hit the scoreboard himself with a team-lifting second quarter goal.

3. Jaspa Fletcher, 6.5/10 -- Lively off half back for most of the day and showed some real moments of composure. He intercepted, won plenty of ball, and offered drive.

4. Oscar Allen, 5.5/10 -- He spent a third of the game on the pine but made an impact when on the field with two goals and clean hands throughout. His three first quarter tackles were a big plus.

5. Josh Dunkley, 8.5/10 -- Could not have played a more inspirational game if he tried. In and under throughout with 14 contested possessions and 12 tackles. Smothers. Spoils. Gut-busting runs. He did everything. Easily could have won the Norm Smith Medal.

6. Hugh McCluggage, 5/10 -- Wasn't nearly as influential as in the preliminary final. Missed a simple set shot in the fourth quarter that would have been scrutinised had the Lions not pulled one out of the fire.

7. Jarrod Berry, 6/10 -- Prolific and under pressure in the back half a lot in the first half. Was less involved as the game wore on but a contributor nonetheless with 17 disposals, six intercepts, and nine contested possessions.

8. Will Ashcroft, 8/10 -- Did what he always seems to do on Grand Final day. Finished with a game-high 31 disposals and nine clearances. Played his best footy in the final term (12 disposals) when the Lions needed him most.

9. Lachie Neale, 5.5/10 -- Enjoyed some clean moments at the contest but for the fourth straight final was well below his best. His third quarter easy set shot miss summed up his afternoon, really.

10. Levi Ashcroft, 6/10 -- Bounced back from an early shaky turnover to have a solid game. Booted a second quarter goal, took seven marks, and had 19 disposals at 90% disposal efficiency.

13. Logan Morris, 6.5/10 -- He was the hero with two goals at the death to snatch victory from the jaws of defeat. Kicked three and set up one of Lohmann's with a clever handball out of a contest.

15. Dayne Zorko, 7.5/10 -- Did a little bit of everything. Had a stack of footy early but struggled to use it efficiently. Finished with 28 disposals and nine marks, as well as seven tackles and seven intercepts.

16. Cam Rayner, 6.5/10 -- Had 18 disposals and more score involvements (8) than any of his Lions teammates and played his best footy late. Should have had a goal of his own in the first quarter but fluffed his lines.

22. Ty Gallop, 3.5/10 -- Looked shaky and totally out of his depth on Dockers spearhead Josh Treacy for much of the day. A pair of late intercepts saved him from a harsher rating.

23. Charlie Cameron, 8/10 -- Booted the first goal of the game (the first of three) and was electric throughout with his speed and cleanliness at ground level. He won countless one-on-ones and was just about as influential as anyone else on the ground.

26. Conor McKenna, 4.5/10 -- Kicked another miracle goal from a sharp angle and set up an important Lohmann goal but wasted a few other chances he'd nail on another day. Was the only Lion who failed to take a mark.

27. Darcy Gardiner, 3/10 -- Not sure he won a contest against Jye Amiss all day. Was beaten time after time and would be copping immense criticism if not for his team pulling off the most improbable late comeback.

30. Eric Hipwood, 3/10 -- Missed a couple of chances in the first half and was held to just one kick in the second. Finished up with a disposal efficiency of 33% from his six kicks.

31. Harris Andrews, 4.5/10 -- Didn't have a disposal in the first quarter, allowed Patrick Voss to kick three on him, and had the shocking turnover that led to the late Michael Fredrick goal. Having said that, he did have seven intercepts and 15 one percenters.

32. Darcy Fort, 4/10 -- Provided serviceable ruck relief to Draper. Didn't have many notable moments, good or bad.

33. Zac Bailey, 7/10 -- Was prolific and influential without being at his devastating best. Set up the important Charlie Cameron goal in the third quarter with a gut-busting run on the wing and snapped a brilliant goal of his own in the dying minutes.

35. Ryan Lester, 5/10 -- Was shaky and unsure early but his 2026 Grand Final will be remembered for that remarkable goal-saving tackle on Josh Treacy. A game-changing moment.

44. Darcy Wilmott, 6.5/10 -- Was a safe and reliable hand out of the back half all day. Used the ball by foot with elite efficiency and won five intercepts.

Fremantle
3. Caleb Serong, 8/10 -- Tireless all game and a beast around the contest. His 13 clearances and 17 contested possessions were both game-highs, as he consistently drove Fremantle forward.

5. Heath Chapman, 7.5/10 -- Calm and composed behind the footy, reading the play superbly and bravely leaving his man to impact contests. Five intercepts. Nearly flawless, aside from one holding-the-ball error.

6. Jordan Clark, 5.5/10 -- Kept quieter than usual but still found plenty of the footy in defence, finishing with 14 disposals and nine intercepts without having his usual influence. Seven turnovers, too.

8. Andrew Brayshaw, 6.5/10 -- Not flashy, but did plenty of the hard work that often goes unnoticed. His seven tackles and six clearances were more telling than his 16 disposals.

9. Luke Jackson, 7.5/10 -- Clearly won the ruck battle with 47 hitouts and 13 to advantage, driving Fremantle's dominance around the stoppages. Also won four clearances, and his two contested marks underlined his influence around the ground.

10. Shai Bolton, 8/10 -- A constant spark and Fremantle's biggest source of X-factor, finishing with a team-high 26 disposals and the Norm Smith Medal. His 58% disposal efficiency and scrappy forward 50 entries stopped this rating being higher.

13. Luke Ryan, 4/10 -- A shaky start featured uncharacteristic fumbles and some nervous moments in defence. Settled somewhat and had a few nice moments, but never had a major influence on the contest.

16. Murphy Reid, 6.5/10 -- A strong finals response given his previous performances, finishing with 21 disposals, six inside 50s, and a clever goal. He was crafty early but then faded as the game wore on. His ball use also let him down at times, with too many missed targets.

17. Judd McVee, 5.5/10 -- Started slowly and was beaten by Charlie Cameron early, but worked his way into the game. Six intercepts and six score involvements, plus a huge fourth-quarter smother on a Kai Lohmann set shot were his highlights.

18. Mason Cox, 4/10 -- Limited to 32% game time so was never able to get into it, with no marks and four hitouts. Wasn't beaten aerially when he was out there, and didn't have an impact outside of two effective disposals when given his chances.

20. Patrick Voss, 7.5/10 -- Played a crucial role on Harris Andrews, keeping the Brisbane star accountable and limiting his influence while making his own impact. Voss took important marks, laid strong tackles, and finished with three goals and eight score involvements from just nine disposals.

21. Oscar McDonald, 5.5/10 -- Another Freo defender who started shaky, but lifted when given more responsibility after captain Alex Pearce left the field injured. Finished with a game-high four intercept marks.

23. Karl Worner, 4.5/10 -- Some useful one-percenters and had 16 disposals with 529 metres gained, but he was outmuscled too often and had a few moments he'd rather forget.

24. Jye Amiss, 6/10 -- Amiss was good after not touching the footy in the first quarter. Finished with two goals from 10 disposals, but crucially won most one-on-ones when duelling with Darcy Gardiner. The Docker won that battle.

25. Alex Pearce, 3/10 -- A miserable afternoon for the skipper, who looked to be playing sore before leaving with an Achilles issue in the third term. Had little impact defensively and struggled to influence the game before that moment.

26. Hayden Young, 8.5/10 -- One of Fremantle's best all afternoon and a class above at times. Young combined his usual skill and power with a huge work rate, finishing with 22 disposals, nine tackles, and eight score involvements, while his two goals in the third term were both massive.

28. Neil Erasmus, 5.5/10 -- Had some clean and composed moments amid the chaos around him, using the ball neatly and generally doing his bit without having a consistent major influence.

32. Michael Frederick, 6/10 -- Worked tirelessly up and down the ground, constantly chasing and harassing his opponents. His four tackles showed the defensive effort, and he nailed a huge final-quarter goal.

34. Corey Wagner, 5/10 -- Played his usual half-back/wing role without doing anything particularly eye-catching.

35. Josh Treacy, 7/10 -- Treacy was excellent around the ground, taking three contested marks and regularly getting the better of Ty Gallop in the air. He finished with one goal but was a constant threat, though a costly brain-fade miss from directly in front in the final term will haunt him.

39. Sam Switkowski, 6/10 -- The retiring Switkowski stayed involved all game and played his usual hard-working defensive-forward role. Remained lively around the 50 applying pressure and creating opportunities while finishing with 16 disposals, six marks, and four tackles.

43. Isaiah Dudley, 6.5/10 -- A constant spark whenever he got near the ball, with 13 disposals and two stunning goals. Dudley took on opponents, dodged his way through traffic and made his moments count, although he had just one touch in the final term.

44. Matthew Johnson, 5/10 -- Had some good wins in and under but otherwise struggled to make his mark on the contest. A missed set shot in the final term was a chance to stamp himself on the game.

stories.headline: Sources: Warriors, Curry reach 2-year extension worth $116 million
stories.summary: Warriors star Stephen Curry agreed to a two-year, $116 million contract extension, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Friday, ultimately opting for a pay cut and security over a max contract.
stories.body:
Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry has agreed to a two-year, $116 million contract extension, tying the franchise legend to the only organization he has ever known through his 20th NBA season, league sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Friday.

The deal includes a player option in the final season (2028-29), according to sources.

The Warriors presented Curry with several contract choices in recent weeks, including the option to wait, but Curry ultimately decided on a pay cut and security over either a max contract or the uncertainty of stalling for more flexibility and information.

Curry is currently on an expiring $62.6 million contract and became eligible Aug. 29 for an extension for up to two years and $136.7 million.

As part of the Warriors' presentation to Curry, the team laid out various paths that included the idea of a slight pay cut from his max, delivering them more salary cap room to build a contender around him in the future, team sources said.

Curry's contract will dip from $62.6 million next season to $55.7 million for the 2027-28 season and a player option for $60.2 million in the 2028-29 season. That will provide the Warriors with around $10 million extra in projected cap space next summer, allowing them to be a bigger player in either free agency or the trade market in the next 12 months.

Currently, Jimmy Butler III ($56.8 million) and Draymond Green ($27.6 million) both have expiring contracts coming off the Warriors' books next summer. Veteran center Kristaps Porzingis has only $3 million of his $20 million salary guaranteed, leaving the Warriors somewhere between $38 million and a projected $55 million in cap space, depending on what they do with Brandin Podziemski's extension eligibility, according to ESPN's Bobby Marks. Podziemski, who has yet to extend, has a $17 million cap hold next summer.

Curry took nearly a month to decide whether he wanted to sign for his full max, accept a slight pay cut or wait to agree to a new deal.

"We're in a very interesting situation," Curry told ESPN earlier this week. "All the different salary cap conditions of whether I sign for a max or less or whatever it is, I want to be on a competitive team. I want to have an opportunity to have some flexibility because we haven't had that in years past, the recent past. ... This team should have flexibility to make necessary moves if things happen. Those are always just the considerations.

"For me, information and patience is key. It's just a very unique situation all the way around based on where we've been the last four years, where I'm at in my career, what our team looks like this year and the absolute desperation to win. Trying to balance all that."

Curry, who said he wanted "no drama" surrounding his contract talks heading into training camp, opted for the pay cut and security three days before the team's first practice, quieting any lingering questions.

Curry, who turns 39 this season, missed 39 games because of a persistent right knee issue last season but said he felt great entering camp.

"The idea of getting back to work is exciting," Curry said. "I feel like I've taken advantage of the offseason. I feel like there's no hesitation about where I'm at physically going in. ... But I'm excited about getting back to work."

The extension brings Curry's career on-court earnings to $652 million, making him the first player to eclipse $600 million in NBA history.

stories.headline: The performance bonuses for Van, Tsarukyan? Spots in P4P top 10
stories.summary: Former UFC champion puts elite status of women's flyweight division on display in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
UFC 331 delivered some remarkable performances, a couple of which landed fighters in the ESPN pound-for-pound rankings.

One of them is not heavyweight Sean Sharaf, despite him pulling off the biggest upset in UFC history with his 12-second knockout of mega-prospect Gable Steveson. Women's flyweight Casey O'Neill produced a leading candidate for submission of the year, escaping a dangerous position to quickly armbar Eduarda Moura, but that didn't earn O'Neill a top-10 spot, either.

Both of those fighters were eye openers, but the rankings were reserved for the two winners of Saturday's headline fights.

In the main event, Joshua Van successfully defended his men's flyweight title against former champion Alexandre Pantoja, using crisp boxing and efficient grappling to secure a unanimous decision. Van moves into the men's rankings at No. 8, and Pantoja, who previously occupied that position, drops out.

Also earning a top-10 spot is co-main event winner Arman Tsarukyan, who knocked out flashy striker Mauricio Ruffy to all but secure a lightweight title shot. Tsarukyan moves in at No. 10, with former light heavyweight champion Alex Pereira falling from the rankings.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Sept. 23. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

T-4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

T-4. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch this past weekend. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: Nov. 14 vs. Josh Hokit

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ will defend against Hokit at UFC 334.

10. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from that challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Mauricio Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

Other fighter receiving votes: Alex Pereira.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Islam Makhachev; 2. Petr Yan; 3. Merab Dvalishvili; 4. Ilia Topuria; 5. Alexander Volkanovski; 6. Joshua Van; 7. Arman Tsarukyan; 8. Ciryl Gane; 9. Alex Pereira; 10. Justin Gaethje.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Makhachev; 2. Volkanovski; 3. Gaethje; 4. Topuria; 5. Pereira; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Van; 8. Gane; 9. Yan; 10. Tsarukyan.

Andrew Davis: 1. Makhachev; 2. Tom Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Topuria; 7. Volkanovski; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Tsarukyan.

Dre Waters: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Volkanovski; 7. Topuria; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Pereira.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Van; 5. Gaethje; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Tsarukyan; 8. Topuria; 9. Gane; 10. Volkanovski.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 8

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Previous ranking: 9

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

stories.headline: Victor Radley cleared, Roosters sweating on Connor Watson
stories.summary: Victor Radley has learnt his grand final fate after a hip-drop tackle, while Connor Watson is hoping to be cleared to play for the Sydney Roosters.
stories.body:
Connor Watson could still feature in the NRL grand final for the Sydney Roosters, with the Tri-colours set to kick off the process of clearing concussion protocols for the decider.

The Roosters were breathing a sigh of relief on Saturday morning, with Victor Radley avoiding a suspension for his hip-drop tackle on Herbie Farnworth in the 36-20 preliminary-final win over the Dolphins.

Radley can enter an early guilty plea and pay a $2000 fine, which would clear him to play in next Sunday's decider against Penrith or Newcastle.

But the bigger headache for the Roosters may be Watson.

The super sub had been on the field for just 60 seconds when his head collided with Dolphins forward Kulikefu Finefeuiaki's hip in the 31st minute at Suncorp Stadium on Friday.

The knock was originally ruled as a category two by the Roosters, before that was overruled by the independent doctor, who deemed it a category one.

That ruled Watson out of the game and triggered an 11-day stand-down that would keep him out of next Sunday's decider in Sydney.

But Trent Robinson said post-game Watson was undergoing more tests, with the coach refusing to rule out seeking an exemption for the NSW Origin utility.

"That was a hard one; he came out as a category two, they changed it to a one after a couple of minutes," Robinson said.

"That's still 'watch this space' on Connor. It depends on how his tests go (if the Roosters appeal), so we'll see how that goes."

Watson is the first player at risk of missing an NRL grand final under the 11-day stand-down run, which was introduced in 2023.

Penrith had faced the potential of a similar situation last year, when Scott Sorensen suffered a head knock in their preliminary final loss to Brisbane.

Sorensen was also deemed to be a category two by club medical staff, before the NRL's independent doctor classed it as a category one.

Had Penrith won the match, it is understood they would have appealed to have Sorensen play in the grand final.

There have been multiple instances this year of players challenging category one concussions and being able to play the next week.

However Watson would still need to prove he was wrongly classified and be asymptomatic from Saturday morning, among several other requirements.

In more positive news for the Roosters, Sam Walker emerged unscathed after a record-equalling 27-day comeback from a syndesmosis injury.

The halfback left the field early with the match decided, but not before delivering a masterclass in orchestrating his backline.

The Roosters have not lost a grand final under Robinson, who will now be angling for his fourth premiership as a coach in the club's first decider since 2019.

"It's mostly internal, you want to get the most out of it," he said of the pressure to return to the big stage.

"I know what my role is ... it's not about getting into a grand final, it's about winning it.

"That's pretty simple and that's what I'm here to do."

stories.headline: Embolo out of Switzerland squad over fake COVID-19 documents
stories.summary: World Cup quarterfinalist Switzerland has lost a second player from its Nations League squad because of years-old cases of fake COVID-19 documents.
stories.body:
BERN, Switzerland -- World Cup quarterfinalist Switzerland has lost a second player from its Nations League squad because of years-old cases of fake COVID-19 documents.

Breel Embolo will not join the squad in Scotland as planned, the Swiss soccer federation said Friday, due to fresh reporting in national media about his past case of obtaining forged test certificates in 2021.

- Embolo: People in Europe 'shocked' at MLS move

- Embolo debut goal gives Atlanta draw at Miami

"This decision aims to allow the team to remain fully focused on the next matches," the federation said about the Atlanta United forward.

Switzerland captain Granit Xhaka agreed with team officials last weekend to withdraw from the squad because he is implicated in an investigation of a doctor issuing fake vaccination certificates during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Xhaka, the Swiss record holder with 152 caps, admitted getting the forged document in 2022 and accepted he made mistakes.

Switzerland starts its Nations League second-tier group Saturday at North Macedonia, plays at Scotland on Tuesday, then has home games in Lucerne against Slovenia and North Macedonia.

Embolo already was suspended for the game Saturday because of his controversial red card against Argentina in the World Cup quarterfinals.

Soccer's Zurich-based rules panel, known as IFAB, later acknowledged Embolo was mistakenly sent off in a breach of video review protocol.

On Friday, the Switzerland Today outlet reported details of Embolo's financial sanction imposed last year for the previously known false test result documents.

At the World Cup, the 29-year-old Embolo scored in Switzerland's opening game -- a 1-1 draw with Qatar -- despite arriving at the tournament days later than teammates because of a visa issue with United States authorities. He also scored in a round of 32 win over Algeria.
