Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season is underway after the Falcons beat the Packers on Thursday night. But what will happen in the remaining 15 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody gives three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

Could the Broncos upset the Rams? Will the Chiefs' Kenneth Walker III and Xavier Worthy score against the Dolphins? Is Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud a fantasy sleeper against the Colts? And could the most entertaining game of the week be ... Raiders-Saints? Let's make 15 big predictions for all of Sunday and Monday's action.

Jump to:

Upset picks | Projected stat lines

Fantasy sleepers, surprises

TD scorers | Other predictions

Maldonado predicts two upsets

Denver Broncos +2.5 (+114) vs. Los Angeles Rams

Denver has the defensive formula to win this. With wide receiver Puka Nacua likely sidelined (groin), Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain II can focus on Davante Adams. Meanwhile, Denver's pass rush can attack a vulnerable Rams offensive line. That pressure could keep Matthew Stafford from finding the rhythm he showed against the Giants.

On the other side of the ball, Broncos quarterback Bo Nix can use quick throws to find wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and avoid long third downs.

Dallas Cowboys +3.5 (+135) vs. Baltimore Ravens

The Cowboys' path is to make Baltimore play from behind in Rio de Janeiro. That shouldn't be hard since the sharpness of QB Dak Prescott and Dallas' passing game gives the team a real chance to score early, putting more pressure on Lamar Jackson and a Ravens offensive line that struggled against New Orleans. The Cowboys' biggest concern is holding up against the Ravens' rushing attack.

Walder predicts three stat lines

Abdul Carter, Edge, New York Giants: 2.0 sacks, 6 pressures, 27% pass rush win rate

Carter's rookie season was noteworthy because, despite just 4.0 sacks, he finished top-10 in pass rush win rate at edge. That was a strong sign about the player he could become, and that signal has persisted in Year 2.

Carter ranks 11th in pass rush win rate at edge and is tied for the fifth-most pass rush wins among all players. In Week 3, Carter gets the chance to run after second-year quarterback Cam Ward, whose 8.8% sack rate since the start of last season ranks third worst among qualifying quarterbacks.

Xavier Worthy, WR, Kansas City Chiefs: 5 targets, 3 receptions, 64 yards, 1 touchdown

Worthy's production has been lackluster to start the season, but that could easily turn around against the Dolphins. For starters, Worthy is a candidate for some positive regression. He has converted only 11% of all air yards into completed air yards, which is an incredibly low rate. And while Worthy isn't strictly a run-straight-downfield receiver, he does run go routes or deep fades at an above-average rate.

The Dolphins have played more single-high coverage than every team but the Browns. That should give Patrick Mahomes a chance to connect with Worthy on at least one outside vertical route.

Jihaad Campbell, LB, Philadelphia Eagles: 13 tackles, 2 tackles for loss

Campbell is close to an every-play role in Philadelphia's defense, and his numbers against the run have been strong. He's in the 94th percentile in run stop win rate and third best in NFL Next Gen Stats' defensive stop rate (a similarly-named but different statistic).

With Bears quarterback Caleb Williams out of this game (hamstring), Chicago could be even more run-heavy than usual. And that ought to present a ton of tackling opportunities for Campbell.

Moody predicts three fantasy sleepers

Dontayvion Wicks, WR, Philadelphia Eagles (rostered in 37.5% of ESPN leagues)

Wicks has emerged as Philadelphia's No. 2 receiver with at least four targets and 12 fantasy points in back-to-back games. He caught 5 of 6 targets for 74 yards in Tennessee last week, and he could see even more opportunities against Chicago since TE Dallas Goedert is out with an MCL sprain. The Bears have allowed the ninth-most passing yards per game this season.

C.J. Stroud, QB, Houston Texans (33.8%)

Stroud has scored at least 16 fantasy points in each of the first two weeks of the season, as he's surrounded by Nico Collins, Dalton Schultz and David Montgomery. This week -- even without Collins (hamstring) -- Stroud has a favorable matchup against a Colts defense that has allowed the third-most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks. Managers dealing with injuries to Jaxson Dart or Jayden Daniels shouldn't overlook Stroud as a streamer.

Adonai Mitchell, WR, New York Jets (28.4%)

Mitchell's role took a big step forward in Week 2, when he drew a team-high 12 targets while playing 82% of the snaps. He has clearly become a major part of the passing game behind Garrett Wilson and has the speed to create big plays. The Lions are tied with the Texans for the most fantasy points allowed per game to wide receivers, and their depleted secondary makes Mitchell an intriguing sleeper.

Bowen predicts three touchdown scorers

Cam Skattebo, RB, New York Giants

Skattebo has seen at least 16 touches a game this season, so we know the volume will be there versus Tennessee on Sunday. Plus, he had two carries inside the 5-yard line in the Giants' Week 1 win over the Cowboys, scoring on a 3-yard run. The Titans' defense has allowed three rushing scores this season.

Kenneth Walker III, RB, Kansas City Chiefs

Walker scored twice in the Chiefs' Week 1 win over the Broncos (one rushing, one receiving), plus he's averaging 23.5 carries and 4.5 receptions per game. Those are big numbers for someone who was part of a committee approach in Seattle. Let's take Walker to score Sunday versus a Dolphins defense that has already surrendered eight touchdowns.

Jalen Coker, WR, Carolina Panthers

Coker has quickly emerged in Carolina's offense, catching 16 of 18 targets for 204 yards so far -- including two touchdowns in Week 1 against the Bears. The Panthers also like to get Coker the ball in scoring position. He already has targets on red zone throws from quarterback Bryce Young, and I expect more on Sunday in Cleveland.

Solak makes four more predictions

Ravens WR Zay Flowers will go for another 150 yards

The Ravens get the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro this week. While I can't speak for the field conditions at Maracanã Stadium, I can speak to a Cowboys secondary woefully lacking in speed and man coverage ability. Flowers is the clear focal point of the Ravens' passing attack, and he should get plenty of free access targets Sunday. He got 150 yards in the first half of Week 1 before injuring his hamstring, which caused him to miss Week 2. Can Flowers knock on the door of 200 in Week 3?

Jets QB Geno Smith will throw three TD passes

He has only one through two games, as the Jets have largely been a run-heavy team and happy to play for field goals. Against the Lions' defense in a dome? I think we'll see a vintage Geno game. Plus, the Jets will likely spread the field out a little more given the absence of TE Mason Taylor (thumb) and the weak spots at the Lions CBs.

Raiders-Saints will be the game of the week

There are a couple of good contenders in Patriots-Jaguars and Rams-Broncos. But I want to see the Saints put together a complete game on offense, and they face a stiff Raiders defense that has impressed with speed and pressure from their front seven. Quarterback Kirk Cousins has made it work without tight end Brock Bowers so far, but the Saints should present the toughest defense they've drawn through three weeks. Give me a 23-21 win by the Raiders, with a game-winning kick to end a contest that was within one score the whole way.

Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. will play -- and shine

The Steelers' star young cornerback has missed the first two weeks of the season with a back injury that might or might not be contract related -- Porter is on the final year of his deal and looking for a market-level extension.

He is back practicing and could play in Week 3, which the Steelers need for any shot against the Bengals' WR duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. For Porter, his best chance at a huge extension -- whether with the Steelers or elsewhere via trade -- is to make an emphatic point against the league's best WR pair.

stories.headline: Barcelona's start to season is best in Europe's top 5 leagues for almost 100 years
stories.summary: Barcelona have begun the season on fire, scoring 36 goals in their first eight matches. How does that compare to the best starts for all time? (Spoiler: Very well.)
stories.body:
LaLiga champions Barcelona have come flying out of the gate this season, with Hansi Flick's freewheeling side picking up where they left off last term and establishing themselves as perhaps the most in-form team on the planet.

Before their campaign was so rudely interrupted by a three-week international break, Barça won their first eight games of the season in all competitions, scoring 36 goals and conceding just eight. That run encompasses seven straight victories in LaLiga and a 5-1 thrashing of Feyenoord in their opening UEFA Champions League fixture.

Just to cement their absurd goal-scoring prowess, the Catalans have somehow managed to hit five goals or more on five separate occasions during those eight games. That is thanks in no small part to the incredible form of winger Raphinha, who has been excelling as a stand-in center forward after his club's summer pursuit of Atlético Madrid striker Julián Álvarez ended in failure.

- Soccer's wildest warmup kits: The good, the bad and the ugly

- Why this international break is longest ever (and that's a good thing)

- 2026 Ballon d'Or: Full men's, women's shortlists, host city, more

The nimble Brazil forward is already well clear at the top of the LaLiga goal-scoring charts with 12 goals from seven games (14 in eight across all competitions) so far. That prolific streak that culminated in back-to-back hat tricks last week, scored in the space of four days in resounding victories over Racing Santander and Sevilla.

After signing off with a "perfect" hat trick (i.e. left foot, right foot, header) against Sevilla, Raphinha can now claim to have made the best goal-scoring start to a season of any Barça player in history. The club captain narrowly pipped the previous record of 13 goals in eight games that was set by Cesar Rodríguez in 1948-49.

Indeed, Raphinha's early scoring form of 12 goals in the first eight LaLiga games of the season has only been bettered once in the 21st century. That was by Cristiano Ronaldo, who scored a frankly astounding 16 goals in eight games for Real Madrid at the start of the 2014-15 season.

Raphinha -- who has somehow missed out on being nominated for the Ballon d'Or -- isn't the only Barça player putting up ridiculous numbers this season. The rejuvenated Lamine Yamal has scored eight goals in as many games while laying on an additional six assists across all competitions -- becoming the youngest player in LaLiga history on record to reach (and subsequently surpass) the 50-assist mark in the process.

In short, things are going well right now at Camp Nou.

Barcelona's performances over the opening eight games of the season have given them a hefty early goal difference of plus-28. It certainly looks highly impressive on paper, but how does Barça's flying start to the campaign compare with the best starts ever made across the top strata of European football?

We've scoured the archives to find the strongest starts made to a season by clubs across the top five European leagues (England, Spain, Germany, Italy and France.) Using the goal difference accrued by a team within their opening eight games (in all competitions) as the defining metric, it would appear that Barcelona's phenomenal start to the 2026-27 campaign is very much up there with the best. But is it the best?

England: Everton, 1894-95 (30 goals in 8 games, plus-23 GD)

The club may not have had much to celebrate recently, but Everton can at least take solace in the fact that they can still boast making the most prolific start to a season on record since the English top-tier was founded in 1872. Sure, it came when Queen Victoria was still on the throne, but nevertheless.

The Toffees won all eight of their opening fixtures in the First Division, including 5-0 and 6-1 thrashings of Small Heath (soon to become Birmingham City) and Nottingham Forest respectively, as well as comprehensive victories over West Bromwich Albion, Bolton Wanderers and neighbors Liverpool. Unfortunately they were unable to sustain their form for the duration of the season and finished runners-up behind champions Sunderland.

By the same measure, the most productive start of the Premier League era was made by the Manchester City side of 2016-17, who scored 25 goals and racked up a plus-21 goal difference after the first eight games of the season. They ended the campaign finishing third in the league, behind Tottenham Hotspur and champions Chelsea.

Italy: Roma, 2013-14 (22 goals, plus-21 GD)

While hardly known for his fluid attacking style, it was Rudi Garcia's Roma team of 2013-14 that made the best-ever start to a season by an Italian top-tier club. The Giallorossi were flawless in the early campaign, winning all 10 of their opening matches to rise to the top of the table.

A handful of impressive victories also came within their first eight outings, including a Rome derby vanquishing of Lazio, shutout wins against Inter Milan and Napoli, and a 5-0 thrashing of Bologna in late September. However, a string of underwhelming draws throughout November and December saw them slip into second place, where they remained for the rest of the campaign.

France: Paris Saint-Germain, 2017-18 (28 goals, plus-24 GD)

Paris Saint-Germain cantered to a domestic quadruple in 2017-18, and it was on the cards from the beginning of the campaign as Unai Emery's side came hurtling out of the blocks. After opening the campaign by beating Monaco to win the Trophée des Champions, PSG hit Metz for five and both Toulouse and Bordeaux for six within their first eight games to leap straight to the summit of the table, where they remained untroubled for the next nine months.

Fueled by the goals of formidable front trio Edinson Cavani, Neymar and Kylian Mbappé, Emery's side scored 108 league goals in total, ramping things up even further in the latter half of the season when they hammered Dijon 8-0, and managed to score seven goals in another clash with Mbappé's old side, Monaco.

Germany: Bayern Munich, 2016-17 (27 goals, plus-26 GD)

Bayern began the defense of the previous season's domestic double in familiar fashion, scoring 11 unanswered goals in their first two fixtures of 2016-17 -- a massive 5-0 win over Carl Zeiss Jena in the first round of the DFB Pokal, followed by a 6-0 thumping of Werder Bremen in their opening Bundesliga game.

With Robert Lewandowski going beyond the 40-goal milestone once again, the Bavarians continued in the same vein from that point, losing just two Bundesliga games all season on their way to comfortably defending the title by a 15-point margin. However, their cup defense ended at the semifinal stage.

It's worth noting that Borussia Dortmund actually scored more goals (30) in the first eight games of the 2015-16 campaign, but alas the club had a slightly lower goal difference (plus-24) than Bayern's high watermark, achieved the following year.

Spain: Real Madrid, 1928-29 (38 goals, plus-31 GD)

With Spain's Primera División not beginning until February 1929, the majority of Madrid's first outings of the campaign came in the Copa del Rey. Los Blancos powered through to the final after marching through four, two-legged rounds that saw them beat Real Oviedo 9-2, Logroño 13-0, Racing de Madrid 9-3 and Athletic Club 7-2 on aggregate, before losing against Espanyol in the final -- all within the space of a month.

As such, Real's first eight games all came in the cup. Technically, they also played matches in the Campeonato Regional Centro -- a long-defunct regional competition that was mainly used as a feeder for the following season's Copa del Rey -- but as that was not a national competition those results are discounted here.

By powering through four rounds of the cup in as many weeks, Madrid racked up a whopping 38 goals, conceding just seven times along the way. Their goal difference of plus-31 was so good that, almost a century later, even Barça's 2026-27 effort (plus-28) can't match it.

In the modern era, a Ronaldo-led Madrid scored 30 goals during the first eight games (all competitions) of their 2014-15 season, but they also conceded 10 goals in that same period to knock their goal difference down to plus-20 overall.

stories.headline: Brisbane Lions produce stuff of football immortality to claim three-peat
stories.summary: The Brisbane Lions etched their name into football folklore and this victory may never be bettered for drama or resilience in the midst of a finals campaign.
stories.body:
There's barely enough superlatives to describe a team good enough to win three premierships in a row. But what about one which not only achieves a three-peat, but does it the hard way three years straight, and just for good measure pulls off the most insane comeback in Grand Final history in the third and final leg?

That's the stuff of football immortality. And that's where Brisbane stands right now, having become only the second club in VFL/AFL history to win a second flag hat trick, following Melbourne in the mid-1950s.

The Demons, though, were dominant right through their second three-flag run between 1955-57. Brisbane has had to pull rabbit after rabbit out of the hat, in 2024 coming from fifth to victory, and last year bouncing back from a qualifying-final belting.

And now, this. Just three weeks ago, the Lions were absolutely smashed by Sydney to the tune of 53 points in a qualifying-final defeat which might have destroyed a team made of lesser stuff.

But what happened subsequently may never be bettered for drama or resilience in the midst of a finals campaign.

First, the Lions recovered their composure quickly enough to put Adelaide to the sword in a semifinal. Last week, they survived a withering Hawthorn comeback, trailing with little more than a minute left when Hugh McCluggage's tackle on Jarman Impey got them over the line.

That would have been more than enough September heroics to make this premiership very special regardless of what happened on Grand Final day. But now we have a win in the most important game of all which will be very hard to top.

A good 45 minutes after the final siren, it was still almost impossible to believe. With only four minutes 18 seconds left to play, Brisbane trailed by 17 points.

Remember that the biggest margin overhauled at three-quarter time of a Grand Final is only 23 points, in 1984. And Essendon had that deficit erased within eight minutes. How Brisbane conjured this Houdini trick is already the stuff of football legend.

Make no mistake. While Carlton's famous comeback from 44 points down at halftime of the 1970 Grand Final against Collingwood remains the gold standard of premiership-deciding revivals, this one, given the lateness of the hour, doesn't pale much in comparison.

The incredible Lions peeled off the last four goals of the game in just 250 seconds. The first, from Charlie Cameron didn't even provoke that much excitement from most of the 100,023 assembled, such was the feeling Fremantle was about to break its premiership duck.

That changed dramatically, however, when Zac Bailey snapped an amazing goal from a thicket of congestion with only another 24 seconds of play having elapsed. And then came Logan Morris.

Brisbane is replete with players who can have done very little throughout the course of a game and still win it. This week, it was the 21-year-old's turn.

Morris had had just eight disposals for 1.1 when, with 90-odd seconds left, he took the single most important mark of the game, a strong contested grab in front of Oscar McDonald. From 45 metres and with ice flowing through his veins, Morris put the Lions in front for the last time.

If that wasn't enough, he made sure of this famous win with a beautiful curling right foot snap from 35 metres. Seven points the difference now, just eight seconds left and game, set and match.

They just don't know how to quit, these Lions. They didn't when they overhauled a seven-goal deficit in a 2024 semifinal on their way to the first leg of this three-peat. They climbed off the canvas again that year's preliminary final.

Last week, they appeared to have blown another preliminary final until conjuring two goals in the last minute. And now a trick to top perhaps anything we've seen on the Grand Final stage.

"We probably thought it was starting to slip away, no doubt about it," Brisbane co-captain Hugh McCluggage told ESPN in the jubilant Lions' rooms after the game. "But we saw last week, this group just finds a way when it gets tough, and in a way it just felt like it was meant to be today after last week."

The sounding of "Wharfie Time" after Patrick Voss appeared to have clinched the premiership for the Dockers might have been a red rag to a bull for the Lions, but McCluggage said the incredible resolve goes back a lot further than that.

"We've done a lot of work over 10 years building our connection, building our brotherhood for moments like that," he said. "And it's a lot of butcher's paper sessions in the offseason, and days toiling down at Coorparoo in the heat, and it all pays off on days like this."

Coach Chris Fagan, sitting among the three premiership cups now literally with his fingerprints all over them, mirrored McCluggage's doubts with less than four-and-a-half minutes left on the clock.

"I thought we were in a little bit of trouble," he told ESPN with characteristic understatement. "The rate at which we were scoring during the game, it didn't look like it was going to happen. But, you know, we've got our strategies in place where if we've got to win the game, we'll roll the dice a little bit and try a few things. We're fortunate that we got the ball out in the middle, which is something we didn't really do all day.

"I just think over time we've just developed a great belief in ourselves. I feel like we're never out of it. So today was sort of like when it all came together, I suppose."

To say that sounded like someone reflecting on the culmination of a long-term project come to a successful conclusion might be an overstatement, but if Fagan does decide to pull the pin on the coaching caper, would any many man ever have gone out more on top than he?

"Oh well, I've been doing it for 10 years," he said. "It takes a lot out of you. I haven't made up my mind yet, but I sort of always had this idea that it would be good to walk away when you're on top rather than walking away when you're going no good at all."

No chance of that now. And what of the team he'd be leaving behind? They'll be in good hands whoever happened to take the reins. Because that coach will know first and foremost that not only is he in charge of the most talented and successful list in the AFL, he'll also be at the helm of a group that just doesn't know how to give up.

stories.summary: New York Liberty (26-18, 13-7 Eastern Conference) at Minnesota Lynx (33-11, 20-3 Western Conference)

New York Liberty (26-18, 13-7 Eastern Conference) at Minnesota Lynx (33-11, 20-3 Western Conference)

Minneapolis; Sunday, 2 p.m. EDT

LINE: Lynx -6.5; over/under is 173.5

WNBA PLAYOFFS FIRST ROUND: Lynx host first series matchup

BOTTOM LINE: The Minnesota Lynx host the New York Liberty to start the first round of the WNBA playoffs. New York went 2-1 against Minnesota during the regular season. The Liberty won the last regular season meeting 93-81 on Sept. 18. Breanna Stewart led the Liberty with 24 points, and Olivia Miles led the Lynx with 20 points.

The Lynx are 15-7 in home games. Minnesota is second in the Western Conference scoring 90.8 points while shooting 47.7% from the field.

The Liberty have gone 12-10 away from home. New York ranks seventh in the WNBA with 20.8 assists per game led by Pauline Astier averaging 3.3.

Minnesota makes 47.7% of its shots from the field this season, which is 2.9 percentage points higher than New York has allowed to its opponents (44.8%). New York averages 10.2 made 3-pointers per game this season, 0.9 more makes per game than Minnesota allows.

TOP PERFORMERS: Natasha Howard is averaging 14.8 points, 7.6 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.6 steals for the Lynx. Miles is averaging 19.8 points and six assists over the last 10 games.

Stewart is averaging 20.8 points, 8.3 rebounds and 3.3 assists for the Liberty. Rebecca Allen is averaging 7.8 points over the last 10 games.

LAST 10 GAMES: Lynx: 6-4, averaging 84.0 points, 33.3 rebounds, 20.9 assists, 7.4 steals and 3.9 blocks per game while shooting 44.8% from the field. Their opponents have averaged 83.1 points per game.

Liberty: 6-4, averaging 85.5 points, 36.9 rebounds, 20.3 assists, 5.9 steals and 4.0 blocks per game while shooting 44.3% from the field. Their opponents have averaged 82.4 points.

INJURIES: Lynx: Anastasiia Olairi Kosu: day to day (foot), Olivia Miles: day to day (calf), Emma Cechova: out for season (knee).

Liberty: Breanna Stewart: day to day (knee), Jonquel Jones: day to day (ankle), Satou Sabally: out for season (head).

stories.body:
Arman Tsarukyan put on a performance at UFC 331 that makes him all but undeniable as the next challenger for the lightweight championship.

Tsarukyan has been in this position before. In January 2025, he pulled out of a title fight because of injury one day before he was to fight for the belt. Later in the year, he was twice passed over when the UFC was booking title bouts. But Saturday's elbow to the face of Mauricio Ruffy gave Tsarukyan the impressive first-round knockout he needed to position himself as the likely first challenger of champion Justin Gaethje.

Tsarukyan's victory also boosted him above former champion Ilia Topuria to No. 2 at lightweight in the latest ESPN divisional rankings.

That is the only movement in the rankings, as Saturday's main event winner, men's flyweight champion Joshua Van, already was the top-ranked 125 pounder. Ex-champ Alexandre Pantoja remains at No. 2.

stories.headline: NRL: Nathan Cleary will play against Knights, but injury 'could get worse'
stories.summary: Penrith have admitted Nathan Cleary is at risk of doing more damage to his injured foot, but insist the superstar halfback will be right to go against Newcastle in their NRL preliminary final.
stories.body:
Penrith have admitted Nathan Cleary is at risk of doing more damage to his injured foot, but insist the superstar halfback will be right to go against Newcastle in their NRL preliminary final.

Cleary walked freely into Panthers headquarters on Saturday morning, moments after his father Ivan declared him fit to play in Sunday's clash at Accor Stadium.

The playmaker's right foot has been the talking point of the finals series, ever since he hobbled through the final 10 minutes of Penrith's week-one win over the Sydney Roosters.

The Panthers have remained tight-lipped on the specifics of the injury, other than to confirm the two-time Clive Churchill Medal winner has a "stress-related bone issue".

"There's enough on (the scans) that there's something wrong with it," coach Ivan Cleary said on Saturday.

"They're not always conclusive as well, so you've got to go by clinical (diagnosis). Where it's: 'How's that feel? Can you walk?'.

"It basically worked out enough that it's an injury that could get worse for sure.

"So it's been a period of trying to manage it the best we can so we can get him to play."

Penrith have a remarkable record of getting injured players to perform in big games, including nursing Dylan Edwards through a stress fracture in his foot for the 2021 premiership.

If the Panthers were to win through to face the Sydney Roosters in next Sunday's Grand Final, a similar challenge would again likely await their halfback.

The Panthers No.7 did complete a session under lights on Friday night, and was also spotted doing some light duties earlier in the week.

After requiring a moon boot on his kicking foot for most of last week, Ivan had suggested early on that his son would need to rely on heavily mental visualisation to prepare.

And while the Panthers coach stopped short of confirming the halfback would be able to kick freely on Sunday, he was adamant he would be able to "play how he plays".

"He'll be ready. He's done a bit of everything," Cleary said.

"He's actually living with us at the moment, so I've actually seen it firsthand how much he's actually done.

"It's crazy. He's left no stone unturned.

"This is what the players dream about. It's why they go through all the hard work in preseason and all the way through the year is to get themselves in this arena.

"They're all true competitors and they find ways to get out there and perform."

The other big call for coach Cleary is whether he keeps Jack Cole at No.6, after naming him there earlier this week.

Jack Cogger is back from suspension and on the interchange bench, and is generally regarded to have a stronger kicking game that could aid the injured halfback if required.

"Coley's just done his job," coach Cleary said.

"He's waited in the wings for a long time. He started last year when Jarome (Luai) left and didn't quite nail it and then sort of went back and worked on a few things.

"Ultimately, he's come in at a big time of year and he's done his job for the team and that's the sort of kid he is.

"He's tough. He plays well and I feel like he's got more confidence over the last few weeks as well."
